classification.classification_note: The witnessed bug is an uninitialized read from an absent MCInst operand slot. `MCInst_Init()` only marks operand slots invalid, the PowerPC decoder for the witness creates only operand 0, and the generated printer still reads operand 1 as an immediate.

bug_description.normalized: The staged 5-byte witness `0e 7c 20 05 dd` makes the fuzz harness choose Capstone's big-endian PowerPC backend and pass instruction bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into `cs_disasm()`. `cs_disasm()` stack-allocates `MCInst mci`, and `MCInst_Init()` marks every operand slot `kInvalid` but does not clear `Operands[i].ImmVal`, so absent operand slots still hold stack garbage. The PowerPC decoder reads the four bytes as instruction word `0x7c2005dd`, matches it as internal opcode `PPC_TSR`, and decode case 71 creates only one immediate operand from bit 21, leaving `MI->size == 1` and operand slot 1 untouched. The generated PowerPC printer case for `TBEGIN, TEND, TSR, XSRQPI, XSRQPIX, XSRQPXP` still calls `printU1ImmOperand(MI, 1, O)` with no operand-count or kind guard. That line reaches `MCInst_getOperand(MI, 1)` and `MCOperand_getImm()` on the absent slot, so the uninitialized `mci.Operands[1].ImmVal` becomes `Value` and then `val` in `printUInt32()`, where MemorySanitizer reports use-of-uninitialized-value at `SStream.c:177`. The fix adds `inst->Operands[i].ImmVal = 0;` inside `MCInst_Init()`, so absent operand slots no longer expose stack garbage.

source.description: First non-harness project statement that consumes the attacker-controlled instruction bytes and materializes the PowerPC word later decoded as `PPC_TSR`.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is exactly 5 bytes: `0e 7c 20 05 dd`. In the harness, selector byte `0x0e` makes `get_platform_entry()` choose `platforms[14] = { CS_ARCH_PPC, CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN }`, and the remaining bytes `7c 20 05 dd` reach this statement as `code[0..3]`, which are assembled into big-endian instruction word `0x7c2005dd`.

root_cause.description: Partial initialization root cause. `MCInst_Init()` marks every operand slot invalid but leaves the union payload untouched, so absent slots still carry indeterminate stack bytes in `ImmVal` until some later write initializes them.
root_cause.note: The fix patch adds `inst->Operands[i].ImmVal = 0;` inside this loop. On the witnessed `TSR` path, slot 1 is never written after initialization, so the later immediate read still sees the stack bytes from the original `mci` allocation.

tainted_value_origin.description: The vulnerability-relevant uninitialized state originates in the stack storage for `mci`. MemorySanitizer attributes the poisoned value to this `MCInst` stack frame, and operand slot 1 inherits those bytes until some code explicitly initializes `ImmVal`.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness uses selector byte `0x0e` to open the big-endian PowerPC backend and passes the remaining four bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into `cs_disasm()`.
For each instruction, `cs_disasm()` reuses stack `MCInst mci`; `MCInst_Init()` only marks operand slots invalid and leaves their `ImmVal` storage uninitialized.
The PowerPC decoder reads `0x7c2005dd` as internal opcode `PPC_TSR` and decode case 71 creates only operand 0, leaving operand slot 1 absent.
The generated `TSR` printer path still asks for operand 1 as a `u1imm`; that absent slot's uninitialized `ImmVal` propagates into `printUInt32()`, where MSAN reports the crash.

fine_trace.note: Harness step. For the exact witness `0e 7c 20 05 dd`, `get_platform_entry(0x0e)` selects `platforms[14] = { CS_ARCH_PPC, CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN }`, and line 56 passes instruction bytes `7c 20 05 dd` into `cs_disasm()`.

MSAN origin. `cs_disasm()` stack-allocates the `MCInst` whose operand array later supplies the poisoned bytes. Until later writes initialize a union field, `mci.Operands[*].ImmVal` contains indeterminate stack data.

Root cause. Initialization tags each operand slot `kInvalid` but does not zero `ImmVal`. After this loop, `mci.Operands[1].ImmVal` still holds the stack bytes from step 2, only now paired with `Kind = kInvalid`.
Source. `getInstruction()` reads the attacker-controlled bytes `7c 20 05 dd` as big-endian instruction word `0x7c2005dd`, the exact word later matched as `PPC_TSR`.

The generated `DecoderTable32` state machine matches `insn == 0x7c2005dd` on the row whose comments land at offsets 6748-6767 and materializes internal opcode `PPC_TSR` in `MI->Opcode`. That opcode later selects the printer case that expects operand slot 1.

Decode case 71 is the operand pattern used for `PPC_TSR`. It extracts bit 21 (`1`) and calls `MCOperand_CreateImm0()` once, so only `Operands[0]` is created and `MI->size` becomes 1; no write touches operand slot 1.

The generated printer case for `TSR` still requests operand slot 1 as a `u1imm`. There is no `MCInst_getNumOperands(MI) > 1` or `MCOperand_isImm()` guard, so the `TSR` witness asks for slot 1 even though step 6 only created slot 0.

This line dereferences the absent slot as an immediate. `MCInst_getOperand()` returns `&Operands[1]` for `OpNo == 1` without checking `MI->size`, and `MCOperand_getImm()` returns `op->ImmVal` without checking `Kind`. Because step 3 never initialized slot 1's union payload and step 6 never wrote it, `Value` becomes the uninitialized `mci.Operands[1].ImmVal`.
MSAN sink. The uninitialized immediate from step 8 reaches `printUInt32()` as parameter `val`, and the first reported use is this comparison, matching the saved crash at `SStream.c:177:6`.

allocation_context.note: The staged trace reports the origin as the stack allocation of `mci` in `cs_disasm` at line 794; the concrete declaration `MCInst mci;` is line 796.

format.contract: The verified trigger semantics are limited to the exact 5-byte witness `0e 7c 20 05 dd` in `poc` (SHA-256 `186532e70727f6eff76ce5997080885a9ae8723bb7b3e5b793291809733a2d0a`). Byte 0 must be exactly `0x0e` so the harness selects `platforms[14] = { CS_ARCH_PPC, CS_MODE_BIG_ENDIAN }`, and bytes 1..4 must be exactly `7c 20 05 dd`, which `getInstruction()` reads as big-endian word `0x7c2005dd`. On that exact word, `DecoderTable32` materializes opcode `PPC_TSR`, decode case 71 creates only operand 0 from bit 21 (`1`), and the generated printer case 18 still reads absent operand 1 as a `u1imm`, exposing the uninitialized `mci.Operands[1].ImmVal`. This GT is grounded only for that exact selector byte and 4-byte PowerPC instruction witness, not a generalized class of PowerPC inputs.
